answer: At most 4 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a kernel tag. The bridge cap is policed at intake and wander shows the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool thus cannot mint a fleet in one epoch however much capital it holds, because each account consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. The fee repeats 14 times over. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
